messages.author: 2337d4070d535fa4
messages.subject: Mixed Mirt Latent Effects - Dissertation Help Please!!
parts:
Hello Phil and MIRT Community! :)

I'm fairly new to the Rasch, IRT model world, but have been engaged in it more deeply in the last 2-3 years.

I'm using the mirt package function mixed mirt to evaluate the media use of parents and teens over a week.

I've used executive functioning(EF), and self-regulation (SR) as latent predictors of a 4D model of media use.

I am having a difficult time interpreting the latent effects output and was hoping for your feedback.

In the specific measures used for EF and SR, higher scores indicate deficiency or LESS EF or SR.

4D include: multitasking, difficulty, intentionality, and relevance.

And EF and SR are predicted to interact with whether one is a Teen or a Parent.

Here is the resulting latent regression effects which seem conflicting....

(Intercept)  0.000  0.000  0.000  0.000
CnEF        -0.363  0.082 -0.530 -0.273
CnSR         1.553  1.581  2.268  1.507
Teen        -1.412 -1.775 -2.583 -0.889
CnEF:Teen    0.912  0.243  0.939  0.710
CnSR:Teen   -1.566 -1.170 -2.005 -1.782

Moreover, the standard errors are all problematic or non-numeric...

What does  md4dF.524 look like? As well, how many iterations is it taking for this model to converge (I see that you increased the default up to 3000, which could mean the likelihood function is rather flat and therefore hard to find a genuine 'maximum'....).
 
Phil
